locked_in: Georgia Power base rates frozen through 2028 (allowed return 10.5%)
The 9,885 MW certified in Dec 2025 (about $16B) is already approved
P.L. 119-21 cut late wind and solar credits; nuclear credits (45U, 45J) remain
weak_links: 4 GW to $660M: rate base per GW from the Dec 2025 certification and a ~10% pre-tax return (estimated)
Chance a Bottoms administration pauses data centers: 10% (estimated; needs the Republican legislature)
KXGA4GW trades only a few thousand contracts

results.hook: Georgia's utility regulators decide how fast Georgia Power grows.
results.event_plain: Georgia approves 4 more gigawatts for Georgia Power

market.question: Will Georgia regulators approve 4 more gigawatts of generating capacity before Mar 1, 2028?
market.rules_summary: Yes if the Georgia PSC certifies at least 4,000 MW of new generating or storage capacity for Georgia Power (aggregate, nameplate) before Mar 1, 2028.

impact.formula: 4 GW x $1.62B/GW (Dec 2025 certification: $16B / 9.885 GW) = $6.5B rate base x ~10% pre-tax return = ~$660M a year of operating profit at run-rate
impact.timing: run-rate around 2030 and later; if No, that growth does not happen

market.p_policy_rationale: A pause likely needs the Republican General Assembly, and the executive-order route is legally uncertain.
market.rules_summary: Resolves to the party of the person inaugurated as Georgia's governor after the 2026 election.

impact.formula: pause removes ~2%/yr of Georgia Power retail revenue growth x $11.1B retail revenue x ~60% non-fuel margin = ~$130M a year
